notes: Do not confuse with مُتْعِب (mut'ib, 'tiring'), which looks identical when written without vowel marks (متعب).
In everyday spoken Arabic, تَعْبَان (ta'bān) is much more common than مُتْعَب for saying 'tired'.

notes: Use 'مُتْعَب' (mut'ab) for someone who is feeling tired. It is very common to express this using the verb 'to be' (انا متعب - I am tired).
Avoid confusing this with 'تَعْبَان' (ta'ban), which is also a very common and practically interchangeable word for feeling tired or worn out.
